T 2 source.c comment.block.c
L  * List of escape sequences used by this program, we do everything just
T 71 source.c comment.block.c
L  * with three sequences. In order to be so cheap we may have some
T 65 source.c comment.block.c
L  * flickering effect with some slow terminal, but the lesser sequences
T 70 source.c comment.block.c
L  * the more compatible.
T 23 source.c comment.block.c
L  *
T 2 source.c comment.block.c
L  * EL (Erase Line)
T 18 source.c comment.block.c
L  *    Sequence: ESC [ n K
T 25 source.c comment.block.c
L  *    Effect: if n is 0 or missing, clear from cursor to end of line
T 68 source.c comment.block.c
L  *    Effect: if n is 1, clear from beginning of line to cursor
T 63 source.c comment.block.c
L  *    Effect: if n is 2, clear entire line
T 42 source.c comment.block.c
L  *
T 2 source.c comment.block.c
L  * CUF (CUrsor Forward)
T 23 source.c comment.block.c
L  *    Sequence: ESC [ n C
T 25 source.c comment.block.c
L  *    Effect: moves cursor forward n chars
T 42 source.c comment.block.c
L  *
T 2 source.c comment.block.c
L  * CUB (CUrsor Backward)
T 24 source.c comment.block.c
L  *    Sequence: ESC [ n D
T 25 source.c comment.block.c
L  *    Effect: moves cursor backward n chars
T 43 source.c comment.block.c
L  *
T 2 source.c comment.block.c
L  * The following is used to get the terminal width if getting
T 61 source.c comment.block.c
L  * the width with the TIOCGWINSZ ioctl fails
T 44 source.c comment.block.c
L  *
T 2 source.c comment.block.c
L  * DSR (Device Status Report)
T 29 source.c comment.block.c
L  *    Sequence: ESC [ 6 n
T 25 source.c comment.block.c
L  *    Effect: reports the current cusor position as ESC [ n ; m R
T 65 source.c comment.block.c
L  *            where n is the row and m is the column
T 52 source.c comment.block.c
L  *
T 2 source.c comment.block.c
L  * When multi line mode is enabled, we also use an additional escape
T 68 source.c comment.block.c
L  * sequence. However multi line editing is disabled by default.
T 63 source.c comment.block.c
L  *
T 2 source.c comment.block.c
L  * CUU (Cursor Up)
T 18 source.c comment.block.c
L  *    Sequence: ESC [ n A
T 25 source.c comment.block.c
L  *    Effect: moves cursor up of n chars.
T 41 source.c comment.block.c
L  *
T 2 source.c comment.block.c
L  * CUD (Cursor Down)
T 20 source.c comment.block.c
L  *    Sequence: ESC [ n B
T 25 source.c comment.block.c
L  *    Effect: moves cursor down of n chars.
T 43 source.c comment.block.c
L  *
T 2 source.c comment.block.c
L  * When linenoiseClearScreen() is called, two additional escape sequences
T 73 source.c comment.block.c
L  * are used in order to clear the screen and position the cursor at home
T 72 source.c comment.block.c
L  * position.
T 12 source.c comment.block.c
L  *
T 2 source.c comment.block.c
L  * CUP (Cursor position)
T 24 source.c comment.block.c
L  *    Sequence: ESC [ H
T 23 source.c comment.block.c
L  *    Effect: moves the cursor to upper left corner
T 51 source.c comment.block.c
L  *
T 2 source.c comment.block.c
L  * ED (Erase display)
T 21 source.c comment.block.c
L  *    Sequence: ESC [ 2 J
T 25 source.c comment.block.c
L  *    Effect: clear the whole screen
T 36 source.c comment.block.c
L  *

T 2 source.c comment.block.c punctuation.definition.comment.begin.c
T 74 source.c comment.block.c

T 72 source.c comment.block.c
L  * called by the user directly in an event driven program. It will:
T 67 source.c comment.block.c
L  *
T 2 source.c comment.block.c
L  * 1. Initialize the linenoise state passed by the user.
T 56 source.c comment.block.c
L  * 2. Put the terminal in RAW mode.
T 35 source.c comment.block.c
L  * 3. Show the prompt.
T 22 source.c comment.block.c
L  * 4. Return control to the user, that will have to call linenoiseEditFeed()
T 76 source.c comment.block.c
L  *    each time there is some data arriving in the standard input.
T 66 source.c comment.block.c
L  *
T 2 source.c comment.block.c
L  * The user can also call linenoiseEditHide() and linenoiseEditShow() if it
T 75 source.c comment.block.c
L  * is required to show some input arriving asyncronously, without mixing
T 72 source.c comment.block.c
L  * it with the currently edited line.
T 37 source.c comment.block.c
L  *
T 2 source.c comment.block.c
L  * When linenoiseEditFeed() returns non-NULL, the user finished with the
T 72 source.c comment.block.c
L  * line editing session (pressed enter CTRL-D/C): in this case the caller
T 73 source.c comment.block.c
L  * needs to call linenoiseEditStop() to put back the terminal in normal
T 71 source.c comment.block.c
L  * mode. This will not destroy the buffer, as long as the linenoiseState
T 72 source.c comment.block.c
L  * is still valid in the context of the caller.
T 47 source.c comment.block.c
L  *
T 2 source.c comment.block.c
L  * The function returns 0 on success, or -1 if writing to standard output
T 73 source.c comment.block.c
L  * fails. If stdin_fd or stdout_fd are set to -1, the default is to use
T 71 source.c comment.block.c
